name: ensemble-two-model-agreement
question: Across every honest full-pack run the two largest gate gaps are verdict accuracy (agreement 0.48-0.65 vs 0.75) and calibration (ECE 0.09-0.2 vs 0.08). Is single-model judgment variance the shared cause, and does deterministic dual-model aggregation fix both?
hypothesis: averaging two independent model verdicts (same v5 prompt, different models) under the existing deterministic tie policy raises fixture agreement >= 0.08 and lowers ECE without regressing invariance or reliability
singleVariable: AGGREGATION ARCHITECTURE: single judge vs two-model ensemble with deterministic score-mean verdict + disagreement-discounted confidence. Prompts, fixtures, gates, temperature, tie threshold identical. Arm implemented 2026-10-17 (scripts/lib/judge-providers.mjs makeEnsembleJudge: strict both-legs, mean scores + production tie rule on the mean gap, mean confidence halved on winner disagreement); execution additionally requires a declared call budget (scripts/judge-capacity.mjs).
executionStatus: BLOCKED - INSUFFICIENT PROVIDER CAPACITY (no declared call budget). The ensemble arm is implemented as of 2026-10-17; do not start until a call budget is declared.
adoptionRule: supported iff usable runs >= 3/arm at reliability >= 0.75 AND target "fixture agreement" moves up by >= 0.08 AND the bootstrap 90% CI lower bound of the signed improvement is > 0 AND no protected metric regresses beyond its cap AND pooled run sd. Fewer usable runs, any unmet condition or missing data => INCONCLUSIVE. Gate thresholds are untouchable.
providerNote: baseline arm runs on unorouter; the ensemble arm adds openrouter as the second independent judge (same v5 prompt; distinct providers and distinct model sizes within the same nemotron-3 family - family-level independence is partial, and the study measures the ensemble the two providers actually deliver)
